conbody.p: A home network is a group of connected devices that communicate with each other and share access to Internet services through a central networking device.
A home network enables devices in a home or small office environment to exchange data and access shared resources.
A typical home network includes a modem or optical network terminal (ONT), a router, and one or more user devices.
In this guide, the acts as the central networking device for the home network.

section.title: Purpose of a Home Network
section.p: A home network provides a simple and efficient way to connect multiple devices to the Internet and to each other.
Users can access online services, share resources, and manage connected devices from a single network.
A home network helps users to:

li.p: Access the Internet from multiple devices.
Connect smart home and IoT devices.

section.title: Common Home Network Components
section.p: A home network consists of several components that work together to provide connectivity.

ul.li: Internet Service Provider (ISP) provides Internet connectivity.
Modem or ONT connects the home network to the ISP service.
Router manages network traffic and device communication.
Wi-Fi Access Point provides wireless connectivity.
Client Devices use the network services.
